sections.heading: What is Interfaces, implements, and structural contracts?

blocks.text: **Interfaces, implements, and structural contracts** is a compile-time TypeScript concept that erases at emit — the run-time behavior is still JavaScript. Interfaces, implements, and structural contracts in JavaScript is prototype-based with class syntax sugar; TypeScript adds nominal-like modifiers but structural typing remains. sections.heading: Why Interfaces, implements, and structural contracts matters in production

blocks.text: Senior interviews and on-call debugging both test **Interfaces, implements, and structural contracts** beyond one-line definitions. Production failures here look like silent data corruption, memory growth, type errors at CI, or async ordering bugs — not syntax errors. If you know JavaScript, use the comparison table to transfer intuition instead of memorizing rules in isolation.
